items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: ever did was, I believe, with me. So, in a way, I broke him into the business.

ctx.x: No, and I kept thinking I would have. But it was different artists represented the guys that – Cal Lampley. Do you remember that name? The first jazz that Teo [Macero]
ever did was, I believe, with me. So, in a way, I broke him into the business. He’s such a sharp guy. He caught on quite quickly.

When I look at your various achievements, there’s so many of them. But there’s one I want to focus on that’s not often talked about. It seems to me that you were very key in moving jazz from nightclubs and onto college campuses. The whole idea – today you look at – so much jazz takes place on college campuses, but as I look at it, you were almost the first. Tell me how that came about.
